newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Argos sees tough markets in H2.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Argos sees tough markets in H2.

text.p: British catalogue retailer Argos Plc is expecting its markets to be tough in the second half and sales growth could slow, as higher interest rates bite and spending of windfall gains dries up, chief executive Mike Smith said on Monday.

"Our markets, we believe, are going to be tough through the remainder of the year...we're not planning for (sales growth) to be as strong as (current levels) through the remainder of the year," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Argos said pre-tax profits for the 24 weeks to June 14 were 28.1 million stg, down from 31.8 million and added that like-for-like sales were up eight percent since the end of the first half.
But chairman Sir Richard Lloyd said in a statement with results that "the current buoyancy in consumer confidence and overall retail sales may not be sustainable."
Smith cited recent interest rate rises, which have added one percentage point to the cost of borrowing since May, as possible dampeners to consumer spending.
In addition, he said, it seemed that consumers had spent windfall gains from building society conversions during May and June and that now this could have dried up.

"Once those windfalls have gone, then there does still appear to be a high requirement...to put most of it in savings. Now it's going to be a question of whether they then release that out at a subsequent date," Smith said.
He added that a lot of windfall spending was "on more expensive products, such as white goods, which we clearly aren't in, apart from microwaves" and other small electricals.
But Argos still expects its second half to be stronger than the same period a year ago, Smith said. "We still believe we're going to deliver a premium growth...in the second half."

The company's performance will be helped by a strong store opening programme and aggressive pricing in its catalogue, where 98 percent of goods included from its spring and summer range will be at the same price or lower, Smith said.
He also cited planned strong advertising and an increase of just over four percent in its range as factors which could help second half performance.

Smith said an anticipated slip of 0.5 percent in gross margin during the second half would not all be due to lower prices but would also be a result of an expected sales mix which was likely to be geared more to lower margin goods than in the same year-earlier period.
He said the company aimed for 29 net new openings this year to bring its total number of stores to 433.

Smith said growth could also come from expanding the group's range and that if stock turn targets were met in the next four to five years, the range could go up to 11,000 products from a current 8,500.
He said that figure did not include a move into any markets in which Argos was not already active and that such a move was not a priority.
"It's all about deepening the range in the markets we're currently in," he said.
He said expansion plans in Holland were on schedule but there were currently no immediate plans to expand further in continental Europe.

But he added that the company's new business development division would be looking at other European opportunities, depending on progress in Holland. -- Jo Winterbottom, London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
